meta.phaseName: Capital structure, balance-sheet risk & returns on capital
assumedContext: Network egress blocked except the search index; indentures, covenant terms and pre-2025 balance sheets could not be retrieved, so the protocol's ten-year ROIC-versus-WACC series could only be built for 2025-26.

Market values of the preferred (~$13.5bn against ~$14.8bn par) and the convertibles (~$6.0bn against $6.70bn face) are analyst estimates anchored on STRC trading below its $100 stated amount and the May 2026 convertible repurchase clearing at 92 cents.
No tax shield is applied in the WACC: preferred dividends are not deductible and Strategy has no taxable income against which to deduct convertible interest.

netDebt in the model block is set to $21,500m - convertible face of $6,700m plus preferred par of ~$14,800m - so that the workspace's asset-base method deducts the full senior claim from gross assets.

findings.claim: WACC is approximately 15.5%: common equity $49.36bn at an 18.0% cost (71.7% weight), preferred ~$13.5bn at an 11.9% current yield (19.6%), and convertibles ~$6.0bn at a ~3.5% yield to maturity (8.7%). No tax shield applies.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived in Phase 4 section 4.4. Cost of equity from Phase 1 (risk-free 4.79% plus beta ~2.9 times a 4.5% ERP); cost of preferred from $1,603m of dividends over estimated market value; convertible cost a YTM estimate on a discounted, deep out-of-the-money bond

findings.claim: Return on invested capital is approximately 0.3% a year: $63.73bn deployed into bitcoin over roughly six years is now worth $65.08bn, a cumulative +2.1%. Against a 15.5% WACC the spread is approximately minus 15 percentage points.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from Strategy's cumulative bitcoin cost basis and market value at 2026-09-11 against the derived WACC. The annualisation is a simple one and is flattered by cheap early vintages

findings.claim: MSTR common is a 1.37x levered claim on bitcoin ($65.08bn of exposure over $47.48bn of NAV) carrying an annual cash carry equal to 3.44% of common NAV. Bitcoin must compound above about 8.8% a year for the wrapper to beat a spot ETF ignoring the entry premium, and above about 12.3% including the decay of today's 1.04x premium over three years.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.unit: % bitcoin CAGR required for MSTR to beat a spot ETF
findings.source: Derived in Phase 4 section 4.4 from the Phase 1 NAV bridge, the Phase 2 carry figure and a typical 0.20% spot-ETF expense ratio

findings.claim: Common equity is wiped out only at a bitcoin price of approximately $20,820, 73% below spot: senior claims of $21.50bn less the $2.40bn USD reserve and ~$1.50bn software business require $17.60bn of bitcoin value across 845,256 coins.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.unit: USD bitcoin price at which common equity is zero
findings.source: Derived from the Phase 1 NAV bridge; static, before any bleed from dividend-funded bitcoin sales

findings.claim: There is no maturity wall, no secured debt and no margin-call mechanism. The preferred is perpetual and cannot be put back; no convertible matures before 2029, with a holder put on the 2032 notes at 2029-06-15. Strategy absorbed a roughly 33% bitcoin drawdown in H1 2026 - holdings falling from $51.6bn to $49.7bn in market value while growing 11% in coin count - without a forced sale.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Strategy Q2 2026 10-Q and note terms; 2032 note offering documents; Q1 and Q2 2026 results

findings.claim: Thirty-three percent of the bitcoin stack already belongs to someone else: $21.50bn of senior claims (converts $6.70bn plus preferred ~$14.80bn) against a $65.08bn asset, accruing at about 11.9% while the asset yields nothing.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.unit: % of the bitcoin stack encumbered by senior claims
findings.source: Derived from the Phase 1 NAV bridge at bitcoin $77,000

findings.claim: Reported results under ASU 2023-08 are a bitcoin price chart: FY2025 net income +$3.80bn on revenue of $477m, then Q1 2026 net loss of $12.54bn on a $14.46bn unrealised markdown - the largest in company history - and Q2 2026 net loss of $8.60bn, for an H1 2026 loss of $21.14bn.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Strategy FY2025 10-K; Q1 2026 results 2026-05-05; Q2 2026 results 2026-07-30

findings.claim: Direct interest-rate sensitivity is near zero - there is no floating-rate debt and the convertibles are fixed to 2029 and beyond. The transmission runs through the STRC monthly reset, which explicitly references credit spreads: each 100bp adds about $105m a year on $10.5bn of STRC, or about $148m across the full preferred stack.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.unit: USD m per year per 100bp on STRC
findings.source: Derived from STRC's ~$10.5bn outstanding and its disclosed monthly reset mechanism referencing credit spreads

findings.claim: A 10% move in bitcoin is a 13.7% move in NAV attributable to common - the 1.37x leverage, symmetric. The premium is not symmetric: peer evidence (Semler 0.88x, Nakamoto 0.70x, Metaplanet 0.99x) shows treasury premiums compress in drawdowns, so a 10% bitcoin fall with the premium going from 1.04x to 0.90x is a 25% equity fall.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from the Phase 1 NAV bridge; peer mNAV readings from treasury-sector trackers and reporting, 2026

findings.claim: The cost of Strategy's largest funding source has risen 33% in fourteen months - STRC from 9.00% at listing in July 2025 to 12.00% in September 2026, worth $315m a year on $10.5bn - through a one-way ratchet. A repeat of the same 300bp move would add $630m a year versus listing, and would arrive precisely when bitcoin is falling.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.unit: USD m per year of added carry if the 300bp move repeats
findings.source: Derived from the sourced STRC rate history (9.00% July 2025, 11.50% spring 2026, 12.00% September 2026) applied to the ~$10.5bn outstanding

findings.claim: The funding gap is structural, not cyclical: roughly $1,608m a year before financing, and a higher bitcoin price generates no cash to close it - it only makes the gap easier to fund by reopening the equity ATM. This is an asset that cannot service its own liabilities in any state of the world.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.unit: USD m annual funding gap before financing
findings.source: Derived: estimated software operating cash flow of ~$25m less $1,603m of preferred dividends and ~$30m of convertible interest

findings.claim: The compression is cyclical with one permanent overlay. Everything about the mNAV gate, the carry ratio and preferred repricing reverses on a bitcoin rally - a 50% move takes the carry from 2.51% to 1.67% of the stack. The permanent change is the spot bitcoin ETF: the access monopoly that once justified a large premium is gone and will not return, so any future premium must be earned by leverage and the issuance machine alone.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Structural assessment combining the Phase 2 carry curve with the post-2024 existence of US spot bitcoin ETFs

risks.text: A 15.5% WACC against a ~0.3% annual return on invested capital - a spread of roughly minus 15 percentage points, with the inflection coinciding exactly with the 2025 build-out of the preferred stack
Thirty-three percent of the bitcoin stack is encumbered by $21.5bn of senior claims accruing at ~11.9% against an asset that yields nothing
The premium is asymmetric: peer treasury companies trade at 0.70x to 1.01x NAV, so a 10% bitcoin fall with premium compression to 0.90x is a 25% equity fall
The STRC ratchet is one-way and repeating the observed 300bp move would add $630m a year of carry, arriving precisely when bitcoin is falling
The funding gap is structural: a higher bitcoin price generates no cash, only easier access to capital markets

catalysts.text: Q3 2026 results: the USD reserve balance, cumulative bitcoin sales and the updated preferred balance - the three inputs that set the bleed rate
Monthly STRC rate resets, each a direct market reading of Strategy's marginal cost of capital
A further convertible repurchase at a discount, or a software-business monetisation to retire preferred - the only deleveraging levers available
S&P Global rating action on the B- stable issuer rating
Bitcoin sustained above roughly $100,000, which restores mNAV above 1.2x and reopens accretive common issuance

conclusions: The balance sheet does not break, and that is a real finding: no secured debt, no margin calls, no maturities before 2029, perpetual preferred that cannot be put back. Strategy absorbed a 33% bitcoin drawdown in H1 2026 without a forced sale, and common equity is wiped out only at bitcoin around $20,820, 73% below spot.

WACC is approximately 15.5% against a return on invested capital of roughly 0.3% a year - a spread of about minus 15 percentage points - and the inflection coincides with the 2025 build-out of the preferred stack rather than with anything that happened to the business.
Thirty-three percent of the bitcoin stack already belongs to someone else: $21.5bn of senior claims against a $65.1bn asset, accruing at about 11.9% while the asset yields nothing.

MSTR common is a 1.37x levered claim on bitcoin carrying a 3.44% annual fee on common NAV. Including the entry premium, bitcoin must compound above roughly 12% a year for the wrapper to beat a spot ETF. That single number is the investment case.

The compression is cyclical with one permanent overlay. Everything reverses on a bitcoin rally except the existence of the spot ETF, which removed the access monopoly that once justified a large premium and caps how high any durable premium can go.
thesisImpact: Prices Phase 3's bleed against the alternative and produces the number the decision turns on: bitcoin above about 12% a year and the wrapper wins; below it, the wrapper loses to an instrument any investor can buy for 20 basis points. It also removes the tail risk that would otherwise dominate - this is not a forced-seller story. Phase 5's question is therefore not solvency but whether a 1.37x levered, 3.44%-fee bitcoin wrapper trading at 1.04x its own liquidation value is worth owning, and at what price it would be.
